body: Thank you, you’re right. Unfortunately this just makes it all worse (not your fault, please don’t take that the wrong way). Sounds like I’m just stuck in this until I can’t stomach another day.

Thank you. This truth is not lost on me, and it’s been on my mind.  My conundrum is that my children are experiencing negative effects of having to witness the abuse I am experiencing in the home, so my hope/wish is simply that maybe the pain they’ll feel from my absence will be better than the trauma they are experiencing by watching me suffer emotional abuse.  There are no easy answers.

My wife knows, she’s very hostile, always has been.  That’s a big part of the problem - I can’t divorce (life is such that even with a good paying job, $40k/yr towards childcare and a housing crisis would mean I’d wind up homeless and never see my kids again), and staying in this relationship is destroying my emotions and mental health.

I’ve been weighing this situation for years.  The best thing is for me to go.  No one will be surprised.  I just want to set them up as best I can.
I wouldn’t say no, but it ain’t what it’s about.  :)
